title: The salah table diagram
subject: Islamic Studies
unit: Summer 1: Salah and praying in congregation
source: Seeded from islamic-studies/y4 lesson 8 (Pupil PDF worksheet: the salah table diagram)
intro: Lesson 8: The pillars of salah (1): intention, takbir, standing and al-Fatihah. To understand the first pillars of salah and why salah is not complete without them

picture.draw: Draw and label: Pupil PDF worksheet: the salah table diagram

questions.q: Put these in order: al-Fatihah, takbir, intention, standing.
questions.model: Teacher: 'First the heart decides (intention). Then I raise my hands: Allahu akbar. I stand. Then I recite al-Fatihah.'

questions.q: What do we say to begin salah?
On the pupil PDF, complete the 'salah table' diagram: write a pillar on each table leg and a sunnah act (such as raising the hands) on the tablecloth.
questions.a: Legs: intention, takbir, standing, al-Fatihah; cloth: a sunnah such as raising the hands or a du'a of opening

questions.q: recite al-Fatihah to your partner, checking each ayah.
questions.a: Al-Fatihah recited in full, seven ayat

questions.q: what is the difference between a pillar and a sunnah act?
questions.a: A pillar must be done for the salah to count; a sunnah adds reward

questions.q: Which surah is read in every rak'ah?
Back to our ponder: what happens to salah without a pillar?
questions.a: It is not complete, like a table without a leg
